title: Court Fracture — Broadcast Championship Split
description: A two-team basketball matchup frame built on a diagonal split background, oversized VS typography, and a monospaced scoreboard strip — engineered to feel indistinguishable from a live ESPN title card.
philosophy: This template exists for the single second before tip-off: maximum tension, zero subtlety. It borrows the visual grammar of broadcast sports graphics — hard diagonal splits, jersey-number watermarks, scoreboard-band type — so that even a local-league announcement commands the weight of a primetime event. It flatly refuses soft gradients, rounded friendly shapes, or anything that reads as 'office slide deck.' The viewer should feel the arena noise before a word is read.
goodFor: Basketball and football rivalry event announcements
Live event countdown slides with venue and tip-off time
Social media preview graphics for matchup hype
avoidFor: Presentations featuring more than two competing subjects or teams
Academic research or thesis defense slides
Brand decks requiring sustained reading or nuanced narrative flow
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should land like a live broadcast title card caught one second before tip-off — the visual equivalent of arena noise made static. Compositional energy is oppositional and bilateral: each half of the diagonal claims its own identity, and the VS mark is the fault line where they collide. Density is front-loaded at the center; the outer zones breathe only because the watermarks recede. Avoid every soft instinct — no eased edges, no ambient glow, no friendly curves; every transition between zones should feel cut with a blade, not faded.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed canvas split by a hard diagonal running from upper-left to lower-right, creating two team-territory halves with no gutter or buffer between them. The oversized VS mark anchors dead-center at the diagonal intersection, scaled to nearly full slide height so it reads as structural, not decorative. A full-width scoreboard band is pinned to the bottom edge — flush left and right, no inner padding — carrying event label, venue, and tip-off time in monospaced type. Jersey-number watermarks bleed off the outer corners of each half at low opacity, reinforcing territorial ownership without competing with the VS centerpiece.

examples.promptCore: Feels like a live broadcast insert card dropped between quarters — aggressive, information-dense, zero ornamentation. The diagonal split cleaves the slide into rival territories, each side owning its data with hard typographic contrast and no visual overlap. Stat figures or callout numbers read like a scoreboard readout: clinical, monospaced in spirit, urgent. Avoid softness entirely — no feathered edges, no rounded containers, nothing that reads as friendly infographic rather than cut-to-air broadcast.

examples.layoutNotes: The diagonal split persists as a full-bleed background layer dividing the canvas into two team territories — left panel roughly 45%, right panel 55%, cleaved by a razor-hard edge at a shallow angle. A 12-column grid overlays both zones; primary content blocks (stat callouts, matchup details, or player figures) anchor in cols 2–6 and 7–11 mirrored across the divide, with ghost jersey-number watermarks filling each panel's outermost column as a texture layer. A monospaced scoreboard band locks to the bottom 12% of the frame spanning full width, housing secondary data labels and a slide identifier pinned to the far right.
